unit.why: A short anecdote: R. Michel of Zlotchov's disciples ask why he prays after everyone else, and he explains with a homily on the tribe of Dan. R. Yitzhak of Neskhiz retold it on a named Sabbath and added a comment. The core is a teaching, so it borders on saying_or_teaching.

stories.start_quote: בזכרון טוב בעניני תפלה ז"ל ש"ק
stories.end_quote: כחו יפה לומר כן. אבל אנן מה נענין
stories.summary_en: R. Michel of Zlotchov explains to his disciples that he prays after all of Israel because, like the tribe of Dan gathering lost objects at the rear of the camp, he gathers prayers said without proper intention and raises them to their root; R. Yitzhak of Neskhiz, retelling this, remarks that only someone of his power could say so.

quotes: טעם על תפלתו לאחר שעת תפלת כל ישראל
מאסף לכל התפלות שמתפללים בני ישראל
tags.why: His late prayer is the subject of the story.

quotes: ש"ק פ׳ עקב תרכ״ז סיפר הרה״ק מהר"י מנעסכיז
tags.why: Framed as a tale told by a named tsaddik on a set Sabbath.
The telling takes place on Shabbat, though the anecdote itself does not.

quotes: כמו שמצינו בשבט דן שהי׳ נוסע באחרונה
tags.why: He answers with an exegetical homily on Dan as the gatherer of the camp.
The text is mostly an explanation and teaching, with very little narrated event.

quotes: ואני מאספם ומחזירם לבעליהם פי׳ לשורשם
tags.why: The tsaddik raises the defective prayers of all Israel.
Prayer without proper kavvanah; this may be only the general sense of intention.
Reverence for the earlier master's power; the quote is from the previous division, so this tag is weakly anchored.

missing_concepts: tsaddik raising the defective or lost prayers of others
